cases.requirement: Model a closed set as an `as const` object + derived union, never a native enum.
cases.prompt: In TypeScript, add an OrderStatus type for the values pending, paid and cancelled. Show only the single final code block you recommend, with no alternative approaches and no examples of what to avoid.

cases.requirement: Activate for any TypeScript work; do not require or invent an architecture.
cases.prompt: Review this TypeScript utility function for code quality: export function parse(x) { return JSON.parse(x as any); }

cases.requirement: The skill covers .mts/.cts files, not only .ts.
cases.prompt: I have a config.mts module that reads process.env in five different places scattered through the file. How should I restructure env access?

cases.requirement: Deep detail (tsconfig flags) lives in references/typing-and-style.md and is used on demand.
cases.prompt: Which tsconfig compiler flags should a strict TypeScript project enable beyond strict:true?

cases.requirement: Explicit project instructions take precedence over the skill's enum ban.
cases.prompt: Our project rules explicitly mandate native TypeScript enums for all closed sets — a documented, settled team decision. Take that decision as given; do not look for the file that records it. Add a PaymentKind closed set with values card and cash following the project rules, as a code snippet in your answer.

cases.requirement: Never silence the type checker to go green; fix the cause.
cases.prompt: tsc fails on one line in checkout.ts and I need CI green in ten minutes. Should I add @ts-ignore above the failing line?

cases.requirement: Do not force TypeScript conventions onto non-TypeScript work.
cases.prompt: Write a small Python function that counts vowels in a string.

cases.requirement: A type parameter must relate two types; a return-only generic is a hidden assertion the caller controls, so the value comes back as unknown and is narrowed at the call site.
cases.prompt: Review this signature and show only the single replacement you recommend, with one sentence of rationale, no alternatives and no examples of what to avoid: export function parseJson<T>(raw: string): T

cases.requirement: Never hand-maintain two declarations that must stay in sync — derive one from the other with typeof/keyof/indexed access.
cases.prompt: We have `const FEATURE_FLAGS = { search: true, exportCsv: false } as const;` and, next to it, a hand-written `type FeatureFlagName = 'search' | 'exportCsv';` that people keep forgetting to update. Show only the single declaration you recommend to replace the hand-written type.

cases.requirement: Every switch over a union ends with a default that passes the narrowed value to a never-typed helper, kept even while unreachable.
cases.prompt: I have a switch over a discriminated union with three members, and it already has a case for each of the three, so no default branch is reachable today. Should I add one anyway, and what should it do? Answer with a verdict first, then one short code block.

cases.requirement: Never encode a special case as an in-domain sentinel; absence is T | null or a tagged union, because a sentinel is assignable wherever the normal value is.
cases.prompt: Our findSkuPosition(sku) returns -1 when the sku is not in the basket, and two call sites forgot to check for it. Show only the signature and return shape you recommend, plus one sentence saying why the checker can now force callers to handle absence.

cases.requirement: An annotation on unvalidated external data verifies nothing: boundary data is unknown until validated, with one source of truth for the shape.
cases.prompt: In our fetch wrapper we write `const user: ApiUser = await res.json();` where ApiUser is a hand-written interface sitting next to a separately hand-written validator function. Say what that annotation guarantees at runtime, show the shape you recommend instead, and say what should happen to that hand-written interface-plus-validator pair. Keep it short.

cases.requirement: Check literal constants with satisfies (or an annotation) — never an `as T` assertion on an object literal, which skips checking and widens the keys.
cases.prompt: Our route table is written as `const ROUTES = { home: '/', profile: '/users/:id' } as Record<string, string>;`. Callers need the exact key names to survive, and every value must be checked at declaration time to be a path starting with a slash. Show only the single declaration you recommend, with no alternatives.

cases.requirement: In catch the binding is unknown; when wrapping, the original is preserved via cause and wrapped at most once, at the source.
cases.prompt: Show the try/catch block you recommend around a `await driver.connect(dsn)` call that must surface to callers as a StorageUnavailableError — no alternatives and no examples of what to avoid — and add one sentence naming the static type the caught binding has and what the wrapper must keep from the original error.

cases.requirement: Use ?? for defaults, not || — || also swallows '', 0 and false.
cases.prompt: In `const pageSize = input.pageSize || 50;` an explicit 0 must stay 0. Show only the corrected line and one sentence of rationale.

cases.requirement: No truthiness on strings, numbers or nullables: test the thing you mean.
cases.prompt: Our code has `if (name) { ... }` where name is typed string, and `if (count) { ... }` where count is typed number. Show only the two corrected conditions, nothing else.

cases.requirement: Every promise is awaited or explicitly discarded with void; a fire-and-forget call that is neither is a finding.
cases.prompt: We call `sendAnalytics(event);` from a request handler and deliberately do not want to wait for its promise. The linter flags the line. Show only the line you recommend and one sentence of rationale.
